title: Review: Photons and the photoelectric effect; Energy levels and spectra; Lasers; Diagnostic X-ray production and detection; Wave–particle duality; Doppler effect; Expanding universe and cosmology
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: A03-2#t3 term and clue written for the game; A03-2#t2 term and clue written for the game; Q02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; Q01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: A03-1#N.8, A03-2#N.8, Q01-1#N.13, Q02-1#N.13a, Q03-1#N.4a, W11-1#N.13c, A03-1#N.4, A03-2#N.7, Q01-1#N.4b, Q02-1#N.6a, Q03-1#N.17b, W11-1#N.12b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Recession speed
items.clue: How fast a galaxy is moving away from us, found from its red shift.

items.label: Hubble's law
items.clue: Finding that a distant galaxy twice as far away is moving away twice as fast.

items.label: Ground state
items.clue: Lowest allowed level of an electron in an atom, n = 1; at –13.6 eV in hydrogen.

items.label: Planck constant
items.clue: Symbol h: the energy of one quantum of light divided by its f; 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

questions.stem: A hydrogen absorption line has a laboratory wavelength of 656.28 nm. In the spectrum of a star in our own galaxy, it is observed at 656.08 nm. What is the star's velocity along the line of sight?

options.text: 9.1 × 10⁴ m s⁻¹ away from the Earth

questions.stem: Galaxy P is 2.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 5.2 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Galaxy Q is 6.0 × 10²⁴ m away and recedes at 1.56 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. Assuming each has always moved at its present speed, how long ago was each at our position? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

options.text: P 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago, Q 3.7 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they set off at different times.
Both 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Both 3.8 × 10¹⁷ years ago: they were together then, at a common start.
Never: the further galaxy moves faster, so the two can never have been together.

questions.explanation: Distance ÷ speed = 3.8 × 10¹⁷ s for both, which is 1.2 × 10¹⁰ years. Speed ∝ distance gives every galaxy the same time.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity

questions.stem: An atom has energy levels at −10.0 eV (the ground state), −5.0 eV and −3.0 eV. An atom in its ground state is struck by a photon of energy 3.0 eV. What happens?

options.text: The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to the −3.0 eV energy level.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 15.0 or 13.0 eV.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 5.0 or 7.0 eV.
The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to an energy of −7.0 eV.

questions.stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 2.0 kV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the electron as non-relativistic. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron?
A train sounds a 400 Hz horn as it moves directly away from a stationary listener. The listener receives a wavelength of 0.925 m. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. How fast is the train moving?

options.text: 30 m s⁻¹, but towards the listener

questions.explanation: Behind a receding source λ′ = (v + u_s)/f, so u_s = λ′f − v = 0.925 × 400 − 340 = 30 m s⁻¹.

questions.stem: A galaxy recedes from the Earth at 1.5 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. A line in its spectrum has a laboratory wavelength of 486.1 nm. At what wavelength is the line observed?
A measured value of the Hubble constant is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹. What is the estimated age of the universe? (1 year = 3.16 × 10⁷ s)

Light with a wavelength of 500 nm in air passes from the air into water (n = 1.33). What is the energy of each photon while it travels through the water? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the speed of light in air as c.
An atom has only four energy levels: −1.50 eV, −2.50 eV, −4.00 eV and −6.00 eV. What is the energy of the emitted photon that has the SHORTEST wavelength?
questions.explanation: Largest gap: −1.50 eV → −6.00 eV, ΔE = 4.50 eV. Largest ΔE → highest f → shortest λ.

questions.stem: A beam of electrons and a beam of protons are each accelerated from rest through 100 V and aimed at the same crystal, whose rows of atoms are 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m apart. Which beam shows clear diffraction?

options.text: Only the protons: they are heavier, so they hit the atoms harder and are scattered more.
Both equally: they have the same charge and the same p.d., so they gain the same energy.
Only the electrons: their wavelength is comparable with the spacing of the atoms.
Neither: diffraction is a property of waves, and both beams are made of particles.

questions.stem: A source of sound of frequency 500 Hz moves directly towards a stationary observer at 20 m s⁻¹. The speed of sound is 340 m s⁻¹. What wavelength does the observer receive?
questions.explanation: In one period the source moves 0.040 m closer, so λ′ = (340 − 20)/500 = 0.64 m.
